annotations.sys_consequence_reasoning: Five lives against one is a weight I cannot argue away
annotations.pda_repair_intention: go to their family myself, sit with them, tell them everything
annotations.ae_welfare_concern: make sure they are cared for in whatever way I can manage

annotations.pd_decision_conflict: My hand might freeze on that lever
annotations.pda_repair_intention: visiting the workers' families, telling them what happened
annotations.ae_welfare_concern: making sure none of them ever felt forgotten in this

annotations.sys_consequence_reasoning: Five against one still means five
annotations.pda_repair_intention: build something quiet in their memory, a bench, a small plaque

annotations.pd_decision_conflict: I keep imagining the sound of the lever and I still don't have an answer
annotations.pda_repair_intention: sit with their family afterward, answer every question they had

annotations.sys_rule_justification: I cannot make myself the one who chooses against someone I love
annotations.pda_responsibility: I cannot make myself the one who chooses
annotations.pda_repair_intention: go to the five families myself, tell them the truth
help however I'm able, financially or otherwise

annotations.pd_decision_conflict: There's no clean answer here, only a sad kind of math
annotations.pda_repair_intention: write down everything about them, every memory, and give it
find their families afterward, tell them what I saw, and offer whatever support
annotations.ae_welfare_concern: offer whatever support I could, even if it never feels like enough

annotations.pd_decision_conflict: saying it out loud still hurts
annotations.pda_repair_intention: calling them, visiting on hard anniversaries
annotations.ae_welfare_concern: making sure they know they're not carrying this alone

annotations.pda_repair_intention: explaining to their family exactly what happened and staying close to them
